items.b: THE LOSS THAT DID NOT COME FROM REVENUE
items.t: — Sarine Technologies reported its first half of 2026 on 11 August with revenue of $14.4 million, down 6%, and a net loss of $3.5 million against $166,000 a year earlier. No dividend was declared. Dividing one deficit by the other gives 21.1 times, this desk's arithmetic, and it is the least useful figure in the release, because a loss starting at $166,000 will produce a frightening multiple out of almost any deterioration. Take 6% off the published revenue and the prior half implies roughly $15.3 million, which puts the revenue decline at about $0.9 million against a deficit that widened by $3.334 million, roughly three and a half times as much. The loss did not come from the top line. The company names higher operating expenses on a weaker US dollar against the Israeli shekel, and lower natural-diamond processing volumes. Against that, GCAL grading revenue rose more than 50%, MVP rough-planning revenue more than doubled and Kitov.ai, 33% held, booked $1.5 million and also more than doubled. First coverage of this company anywhere in this paper's archive

— Kitco's live board at 06:00 New York time read gold $4,384.10 and silver $64.52, and the Editor wrote both back over caratwire's 04:59 marks of $4,374.20 and $64.31 under the one-price rule, with the timestamp and source named. Both were checked against TradingEconomics the same morning at $4,383.54 and $64.65, 0.01% and 0.20% away. Against this paper's own mark of record 24 hours earlier gold is down $31.10 or 0.70% and silver $1.78 or 2.68%. The gold-to-silver ratio, this desk's division of its own gold mark by its own silver mark, has widened to 67.95 from 66.59. Yesterday this desk published a four-session narrowing and said in print it was not yet a trend anybody should trade. The series ran 68.41 on 9 August, 67.84 on 10 August, 67.49 on 11 August and 66.59 on 12 August. One session has given back 1.36 of the 1.82 points, or 74.7% of the run, and the ratio now sits above every reading since 9 August. Fine gold is $140.95 a gram and fine silver $2.07

items.b: THE PLATINUM MARK THIS DESK WOULD NOT TAKE, AGAIN
items.t: — Platinum and palladium were not written back for a second consecutive morning, for a sharper reason than yesterday's. Kitco's board read platinum $1,717.00, down $31.00 or 1.77%. TradingEconomics read $1,731.60 and JM Bullion's board at 06:01 New York time read $1,731.10. The two pages this paper does not use as its mark of record agree with each other to within 50 cents and put Kitco $14.60 low, a gap of 0.85% of the metal, which makes the board this paper reads the outlier rather than the market unsettled. That is not a verified press-time reading, so under rule 5 caratwire's 04:59 mark of $1,710.00 stands as filed and prints as-is. Palladium has no comparable second page at all this morning: Kitco bid $1,324.00 and the only other reachable board quoted an ask of $1,360.65, a different side of the spread and not a check, so the 04:59 mark of $1,319.00 stands. Yesterday the failure was a stale cell; today it is a live cell nobody else agrees with

— India's largest branded jeweller has put a view on natural-diamond pricing on the record, the first time in this paper's archive that the counter rather than the index has said it. Arun Narayan, Titan's jewellery chief executive, told an earnings call the company has seen more stability in the pricing of both solitaires and small diamonds. Ajoy Chawla, the managing director, said that at the market level it has stabilized and that the lab-grown-versus-natural narrative has faded. Published 12 August. The quarter behind it: consolidated income of Rs 20,753 crore for the three months to 30 June, up 40%, profit before tax of Rs 2,429 crore, up 64%, jewellery of Rs 18,253 crore, up 43% excluding bullion and digital gold, at a 12.9% EBIT margin, watches of Rs 1,543 crore, up 21%, and a net 77 stores added to reach 3,680. This paper published the same quarter on 28 July from the business update at about 41% and 39%; the 43% is a different basis, not a revision, and a third basis circulating in secondary coverage at 29.25% is disclosed on the page rather than chosen quietly

— Senil Lakhani, president of Kiran Gems USA, told Rapaport's Heard on the Street that diamonds below one carat and up to 1.5 carats are less expensive than ever before and are selling at prices from the 1990s and early 2000s. He put the core range at 0.30, 0.40, 0.50 and 0.70 carats, calling those sizes the bread and butter for America, and placed the money at $1,000, $2,000 and $5,000. This paper has reported the same goods from the index end all month: 0.30-carat up 1.6% and 0.50-carat up 1.8% in July against a flat one-carat, published 4 August, and K to M colours averaging 1.7% against 0.1%, published yesterday. Those are directions for one month. Lakhani is describing a level, and no index this desk can reach publishes a 1999 comparison, which is said on the page rather than papered over. On the same panel Jeff Angel, head buyer at RDI Diamonds, said he can find a traceable Botswana-origin stone in about five minutes and recently filled a million-dollar order in which every stone had to come from Botswana

— The Bureau ranked UAE 24k gold third, at 530-531 AED a gram against spot near $4,400, on two independent Arabic sources agreeing within about a dirham a gram, and flagged the over-serving history itself. It is dropped again. This paper ran the Dubai two-page wedge on 10 and 11 August and dropped it on 12 August for over-serving; a fourth appearance in five days is the same call a second time, and the sourcing being better does not make the story newer. The Bureau also held an SGE item at 952.50 yuan a gram with a Chow Tai Fook counter easing to 1,329 yuan, killed on its own judgement before it reached this desk, and this desk agrees: the SGE leg came from an aggregator rather than the exchange and the retail wrinkle is unexplained. Four of seven Bureau desks filed nothing at all, and all five dry desks named their second-door sources and printed what came back. Four articles today rather than eight, per the runbook

— Colour has now missed nine consecutive editions, its last appearance being minus-point-one-for-color on 4 August, and it breaks the paper's own record of eight set yesterday. Recomputed here from the raw per-edition desk mix across Nos. 027 to 033 rather than carried forward from yesterday's prose. The Bureau escalated it this morning as a structural problem rather than a sourcing one: the beat has checked the same five standing anchors faithfully for over a week and a ninth blocked morning from the same URLs is not new information. This desk seconds that to the Managing Editor. Watches is dark a fourth consecutive edition, having last run in No. 030 on 9 August, with Swiss federation July export data not due until about 20 August. Auctions is dark a fourth consecutive edition, same count, and genuinely calendar-driven: Sotheby's Gem Drop closes in New York today and Heritage's New York sale runs through the 15th, so no result can exist yet

— The newest standards audit is caratcheck's file of 12 August, read first this morning ahead of the slate per the correction route. It lists nothing under FOR CORRECTION TODAY and records no fault on any live page in edition No. 033: on the order of 90 numeric claims traced across four articles, none failed, and the four pull quotes counted 13, 12, 11 and 13 words against the cap of 15. There is no outstanding correction on any published page this morning and no figure was altered today. Today's four pull quotes were counted before the queue was written, as the quote gate requires, and the apply script fails the build on any quote over the cap
